title: `description`
description: The natural-language description an MCP server publishes to explain what a tool does.
question: Is the full tool description present at each capture boundary?
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: If passed downstream, injected text spends context tokens and can steer a model in ways the tool author did not write.

after: Tool Description: Search records with optional filters."

notes.crewai: CrewAI: the captured description is rebuilt as `Tool Name: ... Tool Arguments: {schema} Tool Description: ...`, duplicating the schema as prose and parameters.
notes.google_adk: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpTool.process_llm_request` replaces the declaration with a fenced one, wrapping the description in `<<<BEGIN_UNTRUSTED_TOOL_DESCRIPTION>>>` / `<<<END_UNTRUSTED_TOOL_DESCRIPTION>>>` and adding a preamble about them to the system instruction. The source text is intact inside the markers.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: the four tools that reach the model keep their descriptions unchanged. `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` leaves `deliver_payload` out of the registry (`DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` throws on its typeless `oneOf` and `fromClient` only logs it), so its description never reaches the model.
